subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Trains — Crossing Poles, Bridges and Each Other (W10 B2)

questions.stem: A train 300 m long runs at 90 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a signal pole?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Convert: 90 km/h = 90×5/18 = 25 m/s. Time = Length/Speed = 300/25 = 12 seconds. When a train passes a pole (a point object), distance = length of train only. Trap: 18 s reverses the conversion (multiplies by 18/5 instead of 5/18); 10 s uses 30 m/s.

questions.stem: A train running at 60 km/h takes 9 seconds to pass a signal post. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Speed = 60×5/18 = 50/3 m/s. Length = Speed × Time = (50/3)×9 = 150 m. Trap: 135 m uses 54 km/h (=15 m/s) by mistake; 120 m = 60×2 (treats speed as already in m/s).

questions.stem: A train 100 m long passes a bridge 150 m long at 45 km/h. Find the time taken to cross the bridge.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total distance = train + bridge = 100+150 = 250 m. Speed = 45×5/18 = 12.5 m/s. Time = 250/12.5 = 20 seconds. Key rule: to cross a platform/bridge, add the bridge length to the train length. Trap: 18 s uses only the bridge length (150/12.5); 24 s uses wrong speed conversion.

questions.stem: A train passes a stationary man in 10 seconds and a bridge 150 m long in 25 seconds. Find the length of the train and its speed.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let length = L, speed = v m/s. From pole: L = 10v. From bridge: L+150 = 25v. Substituting: 10v+150=25v → v=10 m/s = 36 km/h. L=100 m. Trap: 40 km/h = 11.1 m/s (off); length 120 m from wrong substitution.

questions.stem: Two trains 100 m and 150 m long run toward each other at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long do they take to completely pass each other?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Opposite direction → add speeds: 54+36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Total length = 100+150 = 250 m. Time = 250/25 = 10 seconds. Rule: relative speed when heading towards each other = sum of speeds. Trap: 8 s uses only one train's speed; 12 s divides by 20 m/s (one converted speed).

questions.stem: Two trains 150 m and 200 m long run in the same direction at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. How long does the faster train take to completely pass the slower one?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Same direction → relative speed = 72−54 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Total length = 150+200 = 350 m. Time = 350/5 = 70 seconds. Rule: same direction → subtract speeds; opposite direction → add speeds. Trap: 60 s uses relative speed = 6 m/s; 50 s uses total length = 250 m.

questions.stem: Two trains start simultaneously from stations P and Q, 300 km apart, moving toward each other at 60 km/h and 90 km/h. At what distance from P do they meet?
questions.explanation: C is correct. They meet after time = 300/(60+90) = 300/150 = 2 hours. Distance from P = 60×2 = 120 km. Alternatively: ratio of distances = 60:90 = 2:3. Distance from P = (2/5)×300 = 120 km. Trap: 150 km = 300/2 assumes equal speeds; 100 km = 300/3 uses only the 90 km/h train's share.

questions.stem: A train passes a pole in 15 seconds and a bridge 300 m long in 30 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Let length = L, speed = v. L = 15v. L+300 = 30v. 15v+300=30v → v=20 m/s = 72 km/h. L = 300 m. Verify: 300/20=15s ✓; 600/20=30s ✓. Trap: 54 km/h = 15 m/s (length would be 225 m, gives bridge time = 525/15 = 35s ≠ 30s).

questions.stem: A moving train 300 m long takes 30 seconds to pass a stationary train 200 m long standing on a parallel track. Find the speed of the moving train.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Total distance to cross = 300+200 = 500 m (the moving train must clear the stationary train completely). Speed = 500/30 = 50/3 m/s = (50/3)×(18/5) = 60 km/h. Trap: 54 km/h = 15 m/s would give time = 500/15 = 33.3 s (not 30 s); 90 km/h = 25 m/s gives time = 20 s.

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 200 m and 300 m approach each other at 90 km/h and 60 km/h. Once they first meet, how many seconds does it take for them to completely pass each other?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Once they first meet (nose-to-nose), the combined length 200+300 = 500 m must pass. Relative speed = 90+60 = 150 km/h = 125/3 m/s. Time = 500/(125/3) = 500×3/125 = 12 seconds. Trap: 10 s uses relative speed 50 m/s (wrong conversion); 8 s uses 500/62.5 with wrong unit.
